newsitem.title: USA: Butler sees lower '97 oper earnings vs '96.
newsitem.headline: Butler sees lower '97 oper earnings vs '96.

text.p: Butler Manufacturing Co said Wednesday it expects net operating earnings for the full year 1997 will be slightly lower than last year's.
"We expect a strong third quarter and second half for all of our businesses," Robert West, chairman and chief executive, said in a statement.

"However, because of larger-than-anticipated first half losses in Europe and the absence of our recently sold grain systems business, Butler's full year net operating earnings will likely be slightly lower than the $3.35 per share we earned a year ago," he added.
Butler said total backlog on June 30 was $301 million, up six percent from last year. Product backlog was up 12 percent and construction backlog was down 15 percent.
On Wednesday Butler reported second quarter earnings of $0.74 a share excluding a $1.72 a share gain on the sale of its Grain Systems business. Second quarter 1996 earnings were $0.75 a share.

Butler said sales at its new subsidiaries in China and Brazil were good, and backlog at both units is on plan. The company said it expects both operations to become profitable during the second half of the year.

Its European metal building systems business posted a larger loss in the first half of 1997 than in the first half of 1996. The larger loss was almost entirely because of the strength of the British pound against the German mark, the company said.
Butler produces pre-engineered building systems and supplies specialty components and construction services.
